title: Principal Stratum Effects across Trials under Total-Variation Relaxations of Transition Transportability
banked_reason: Cold D0.5 review: subfield tier, below the fixed field floor; sound positive-radius core, but the finite determining-ray clause and Charnes-Cooper cited leaf require local repair and the field lift requires new theorem architecture.
gap_reasons: The finite set is defined to contain only facet-normal rays, but at d=0 (and other lower-dimensional images) compatibility also requires affine-hull equalities; treating each equality as two supporting half-spaces in the proof does not put their non-facet normals in R*, so its advertised finite facet test can accept nu outside P_{mu,d}.

The supplied attested sentence only says that a problem with 'X regular' reduces to two LPs; it does not state the core claim's arbitrary-polyhedron/strict-denominator hypotheses or optimizer-recovery conclusion.
Cold tier verdict: review_general tier=subfield, meets_floor=false, novelty_target=field, floor=field, paper_score_ceiling=7.2, salvageable=true.
Tier-lifting characterization is not bounded: it requires new endpoint-reaching radius definitions, a replacement flagship theorem, and a new proof absent from durable state.
proof_attempt_summary: Seven proposal versions replaced the original interior-floor formula with primitive stochastic kernels, positioned Wu–Mao as the d=0 baseline, and derived positive-radius PSACE, sign-radius, and CAD-profiling results. The final cold review judged the contribution subfield rather than field and found that the finite facet-normal test omits affine-hull equality normals; the Charnes–Cooper cited leaf was also broader than its attestation, although the needed compact endpoint case was proved directly. A future reuse should first repair those two local defects, then supply a genuinely new saturation-radius or similarly anchor-free flagship theorem before seeking field status.
tldr: The model relaxes Wu and Mao's transition restriction by coupling randomized ACCT trials through one shared stochastic center and primitive trial-specific stochastic rows within rowwise TV distance \(d\), with exact marginal reproduction. The radius \(d\) is a prespecified sensitivity parameter for latent cross-world rows, not a feature identified by randomized-arm marginals. The headline results give attained coupled PSACE intervals, an explicit nondegenerate observable class on which every \(0<d\le10^{-2}\) strictly enlarges the Wu--Mao point while remaining strictly sharper than separate-trial bounds, and a global sign radius characterized by an independent primal--dual cut system with rational certificates and a \(+\infty\) branch. Direct polyhedral support supplies compatibility, and an observable first stage bounds every denominator. One maintained multinomial region gives simultaneous coverage with incompatible candidate marginals retained. Exact finite profiling exists by cylindrical algebraic decomposition for rational numerical inputs; practically tractable complexity, implementation, and the numerical ACCT reanalysis remain open.
gap: Wu and Mao point-identify four-state joint potential-outcome laws and PSACEs under exact transition transportability and full column rank, but do not characterize partial identification under a positive rowwise-TV relaxation. Jiang, Ding, and Geng identify PSACEs under a different exact cross-trial homogeneity restriction and give separate-trial bounds without monotonicity; Yuan, Feller, and Miratrix use a site-level zero-correlation restriction; Wu and Antonelli use continuous-intermediate outcome models with sign or dominant-observed-effect restrictions. Miratrix and coauthors and Long and Hudgens tighten principal-effect bounds using predictive baseline covariates under principal-stratum restrictions including monotonicity, while Trangucci, Chen, and Zelner obtain multicenter point identification from proxies, homogeneity, misclassification, and rank. The surrogate-resilience and historical-prediction comparators target different objects. None gives an attained positive-TV PSACE frontier together with a finite dual distance-to-sign-reversal certificate.
fill: Randomization and consistency identify the kernel-class marginals from observed-arm laws, while conditional multinomial sampling supplies concentration. The direct rowwise support LP characterizes compatibility; linear-fractional programs attain endpoints over the full prespecified \(d\)-path; an explicit open observable neighborhood gives strict intermediate identification for every \(0<d\le10^{-2}\); and a canonical primal--dual sign program returns an adversarial kernel or a finite rational certificate. One maintained multinomial region gives simultaneous coverage by inclusion, and \(\rho^*\) remains only the smallest data-compatible radius.
